referenceFunction.generalComment: This dataset represents the activity of waste disposal of liquid crystal display in a municipal solid waste incinerator (MSWI) Recommended use of this dataset: Only for incineration of LCD modules (mostly glass and inorganics, some electronic components, copper and plastics) generated in the recycling (mechanical treatment) of LCD screens (Liquid Crystal Display screen residue) Inventoried waste contains 0.87% Plastics from electronic consumer goods; 0.87% Plastics from electronic industrial goods; 82% Glass; 0.87% wiring copper; 0.83% liquid crystals; 0.12% ITO coating; 14.5% electronic goods; . Waste composition (wet, in ppm): upper heating value 2.835 MJ/kg; lower heating value 2.551 MJ/kg; H2O 40144; O 430500; H 7674.6; C 63365; S 102.58; N 1270.5; P 46.362; B 0.0082045; Cl 1519.4; Br 95.711; F 11.587; I n.a.; Ag 30.387; As 0.1305; Ba 8.0249; Cd 10.593; Co 0.51291; Cr 317.5; Cu 26895; Hg 0.16101; Mn 71.044; Mo 0.56082; Ni 1905; Pb 4347.4; Sb 112.38; Se 0.034097; Sn 2351.8; V 0.01305; Zn 2573.8; Be 0.0081182; Sc n.a.; Sr 1.4369; Ti 77.9; Tl 0.0064946; W n.a.; Si 294410; Fe 5671.6; Ca 60879; Al 900.8; K 965.57; Mg 2.0446; Na 52850; Share of carbon in waste that is biogenic 0%. Share of metals in waste not oxidised and bulk-recyclable (exclude very small or thin parts) Iron: 99.52%; Alu: 57.22%; Copper: 99.77%. One kg of this waste produces 0.9804 kg of slag and 0.01217 kg of residues, which are landfilled. Additional solidification with 0.004869 kg of cement. Net energy production: 0.24MJ/kg electric energy and 0.64MJ/kg thermal energy. Recovery of metal scrap to recycling: 3.1738g iron scrap, 0.131g aluminium scrap, 7.6938g copper scrap.;; UUID: 67ab7964-00b2-41d5-9ff1-1aa29b2354ea
referenceFunction.includedProcesses: Waste incineration from waste reception gate further downstream (excluding transport to the MSWI plant). Waste-specific air and water emisions from incineration, auxiliary material consumption for flue gas cleaning. Short-term emissions to river water and long-term emisisons to ground water from slag compartment (from bottom ash) and residual material landfill (from solidified fly ashes and scrubber slugde). Waste-specific process energy demands for MSWI and net energy generation.
referenceFunction.localName: Disposal, LCD module, to municipal waste incineration
referenceFunction.name: Disposal, LCD module, to municipal waste incineration

geography.text: Specific to the technology mix encountered in Switzerland in 2010. Well applicable to modern incineration practices in Europe, North America or Japan.

technology.text: average Swiss MSWI plants in 2010 (grate incinerators) with electrostatic precipitator for fly ash (ESP), wet flue gas scrubber and 25% SNCR , 42.77% SCR-high dust , 32.68% SCR-low dust -DeNOx facilities and 0% without Denox (weighted according to mass of burnt waste, representing Swiss average). Efficiency of iron scrap separation from slag : 58%. Efficiency of non-ferrous scrap separation from slag : 31%. Gross electric efficiency technology mix 15.84% and Gross thermal efficiency technology mix 28.51%

timePeriod.text: Waste composition as given in literature reference, theoretical data or other source. Transfer coefficients for modern MSWI.

representativeness.extrapolations: Typical elemental transfer coefficients from current studies for modern MSWI, completed with data from coal power plants and estimates, adapted for inert/burnable waste.
representativeness.samplingProcedure: fully waste-specific calculation based on literature data for average MSWI operation performance
representativeness.uncertaintyAdjustments: uncertainty of waste input composition data derived from generic formula GSD(c) = N*ln(c)+1
